query: What patient needs appear in visit notes?

per_column.name: clinical_problem_type
per_column.rationale: Strong categorical axis directly answering 'what patient needs appear'. Values well-grounded (annual physical=preventive, cough/fever=acute, post-MI follow-up=chronic). Acne classified as chronic_disease_management is defensible.

per_column.name: acuity_complexity
per_column.rationale: Useful severity axis for grouping. Somewhat correlated with existing 'urgency' but adds finer clinical gradation. Grounding mostly sound; the annual-physical row as low_acuity is fine, but acuity labels partly infer beyond explicit text.

per_column.name: care_action_required
per_column.rationale: Directly captures actionable needs, high analytical leverage. Values track text well (labs ordered, monitoring, medication initiation, MRI). Sound extraction.

per_column.name: specialist_involvement
per_column.rationale: Useful for grouping, but values essentially mirror the existing 'department' column, making it partly redundant. Grounded via department mapping.

per_column.name: diagnostic_workup_need
per_column.rationale: Genuine new axis on workup needs. Mostly grounded, but the annual-physical row (lipid panel + HbA1c, both labs) labeled 'multi_modal' overstates modality diversity; a minor inconsistency.

per_column.name: medication_need_type
per_column.rationale: Distinct, valuable medication axis. NULL/absent handled correctly for silent rows. Values grounded (statin=chronic, doxycycline=new_prescription).

per_column.name: preventive_or_wellness_need
per_column.rationale: Useful preventive axis, mostly correct with 'not_present' for silent rows. But the annual-physical row labeled 'chronic_disease_prevention' is an unwarranted specific; the text describes routine screening, not stated chronic disease prevention.

per_column.name: specialist_or_ancillary_involvement
per_column.rationale: Exact duplicate of 'specialist_involvement' (identical top values and row values); a mere restatement adding no analytical leverage.

judge.rationale: Most columns provide genuine, distinct analytical axes (problem type, acuity, care action, workup, medication, prevention) that directly serve the query about patient needs and are largely well-grounded in the visit notes. Deductions: specialist_or_ancillary_involvement is a verbatim duplicate of specialist_involvement (no leverage), and both specialist columns largely restate the existing department field. Minor grounding issues appear in over-specific labels (e.g., annual physical tagged chronic_disease_prevention and multi_modal workup for two lab tests). Silent-row 'not_present'/NULL values are handled correctly and not penalized.
